notes:
Account overview: CodeTide builds an enterprise-grade PR assistant used inside IDE and CI. Primary product: 'Wave' — auto-diff summaries, line-level comment suggestions, and ranked actionable suggestions for reviewers. They are deeply latency-sensitive (developers want streaming in-editor completions while reviewing diffs) and want model pinning per product branch.

Discovery notes (highlights):
- 2025-11-02 initial inbound: sign-up via quickstart, interested in replacing internal heuristics + heuristics -> LLM for PR triage.
- 2025-11-09 discovery call with Maya (AE) + Andre (SE): demoed streaming low-latency completions; customer asked about 50ms token latency and prefix caching for repeated repository contexts.
- 2026-01-12 security questionnaire submitted; flagged retention and audit logging needs. They require SOC2 and SSO (SAML).
- 2026-02-14 call (ff_2026-02-14_6620): product + infra team; discussed private VPC connector, repo access model (read-only), and on-the-fly model pinning per repo branch for reproducible suggestions.
- 2026-03-01 scoping call (ff_2026-03-01_7691): agreed on 6-week POC, success metrics: 85% reviewer acceptance rate on suggested comments, median diff-summary latency <2s for diffs up to 200 LOC, cost per PR < $0.15 on average.

Technical requirements noted:
- Workloads: PR diff summarization (batch + streaming), in-IDE comment generation (streaming), reranking of candidate comments, embeddings for search and fuzzy match.
- Latency/throughput targets: median end-to-end summary <2s (200 LOC), streaming tokens in-editor under 100ms first-byte where possible, target 500 concurrent reviewers on Dedicated pool.
- Model preferences: open-model family with ability to pin versions to release tags; quantized variants acceptable if quality within 3% of baseline.
- Routing/fallback: prefer fast hosted variant with automatic fallback to lower-cost model if Dedicated pool saturated; need deterministic fallback policy.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, per-repo rollup usage.

POC plan (agreed):
- Week 0: exchange SSO metadata, grant read-only GitHub Enterprise access, sign form for security scoping.
- Week 1-2: integrate repo connector + run 100 sample PRs through hosted API for baseline metrics.
- Week 3-4: deploy Dedicated sandbox (small GPU pool) for latency testing and model pinning proof.
- Week 5-6: A/B testing against their rule-based comment generator; collect reviewer acceptance and cost metrics.

Quotes / customer language captured:
- "We need reproducible suggestions tied to branch pins — security + auditability is non-negotiable."
- "If the suggestion appears in the IDE with a lag, adoption will tank. Streaming is table stakes."

Deal health / risks:
- Champion: Head of Developer Productivity (internal), high alignment.
- Procurement timeline: Legal + security cycles likely push to April.
- Primary blockers: legal on retention, cost spikes for heavy CI runs, final SSO metadata.

Sales actions open:
- AE: follow up with contract rider language for code retention + deletion window.
- SE: prepare reproducible model-pinning demo (branch -> model-version mapping).
- Infra: validate VPC connector designs and write short-run cost estimator for 1-month projected tokens.

Short snippet of recent internal notes (choppy CRM style):
- 2026-03-09: Demo with eng leads — liked reranking UI but asked for more deterministic explainability on why a comment ranked #1. SE action: wire up debug traces.
- 2026-03-05: Legal requested clause for ephemeral KV cache deletion. Looping in partnerships counsel.
- 2026-02-20: Ran 50 PRs through hosted API; median summary latency 1.9s, but 95th pctl 4.8s on large diffs. Need batching adjustments and prefix caching.

Attachments and next actions referenced above. POC start contingent on signed SOW and SSO metadata.
